page: Microsoft Azure EC20as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on AMD EPYC 9V74 processors within the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 10 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The processor configuration features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, supporting cryptographic instruction extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI alongside AVX instructions. It is configured with 160.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

The EC20as_v5 includes no bundled local storage and requires remote Azure Premium Storage for persistent operating system and data volumes. Across synthetic benchmarks, compute and memory throughput metrics place the instance consistently within the middle 50% average category. Evaluated performance figures include a PassMark CPU score of 23,423.54, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,339.0, and a PassMark memory score of 2,224.13. In-memory data handling capacity is demonstrated by benchmark results showing 19.05 million Redis SET operations per second alongside a PassMark database score of 7,495.77.

From an operational cost and resource efficiency perspective, the EC20as_v5 delivers high memory density per compute unit without the overhead of hardware accelerators, containing zero GPUs. The absence of local disk drives simplifies stateless horizontal scaling patterns, though input and output latency depends entirely on network-attached storage configurations. This hardware balance makes the instance appropriate for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory caching systems, relational database management systems, enterprise resource software, and moderate analytics pipelines.
